text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Sam Nujoma told visiting U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Saturday he would send troops to Zaire if the U.N. commits a peacekeeping mission to help oversee an end to the civil war there.
- The Namibian government could be losing millions through customs duty evasion and loopholes in the granting of Duty Credit Certificates, an investigation by the newspaper found.

- President Nujoma has pardoned 1,212 prisoners, including all those whose conditional release on parole in 1997 was approved on or before March 21 this year, as well as first time offenders serving sentences of not more than two years.
